children: , the AI-connectivity and custom-silicon supplier, unveiled three 2-nanometer optical technologies aimed squarely at one of AI infrastructure's biggest pressure points: moving more data through increasingly crowded networks. Shares climbed approximately 3.4% to $252.39 Monday.

The lineup stretches from 400-gigabit-per-second-per-lane PAM4 technology built for 3.2-terabit connectivity to an 800-gigabit ZR/ZR+ pluggable with integrated MACsec encryption and 1.6-terabit coherent links spanning data-center connections. Marvell is also showing a 102.4-terabit-per-second co-packaged-optics platform among 38 demonstrations at ECOC. The valuation picture is much hotter than the operating story: the shares at $252.39 sit 109.07% above the $120.72 GF Value, signaling that investors are already pricing in a substantial amount of future growth.

That optimism has some operating support. Marvell's latest quarter produced $2.739 billion of revenue, up 37%, while data-center sales jumped 46%. But demonstrations are not revenue. The next test is execution: customer design wins, production schedules, shipment volumes and margins will decide whether Marvell's expanding optical portfolio can grow fast enough to justify a stock already trading far above its GF Value estimate.

title: Marvell Rises Over 3.3% as 2-Nanometer Optics Target AI's Copper Wall
